insight.title: Why You Catch Up Faster by Slowing Down
insight.subtitle: How reducing your speed helps you reach your goals sooner.

sections.text: To catch an object in orbit, you don’t aim at it and accelerate. You slow down. This drop in velocity lowers your altitude, which actually increases your speed relative to the earth below.

We treat deadlines like targets we must chase with force. But high-pressure acceleration clouds judgment. By lowering your intensity, you drop into a "lower orbit" where you can finally see the path clearly.
This is about efficiency, not laziness. When you stop rushing, you stop creating the mistakes that usually slow you down. You reach the destination sooner simply by refusing to chase it recklessly.
Try this today: When you feel rushed to finish a task today, pause for ten seconds to check your direction.
True speed is the absence of unnecessary friction.

news.title: Delta raises checked baggage fees as the Iran war drives up jet fuel prices
news.description: Delta Air lines is joining a growing list of U.S. carriers raising checked bag fees. The move announced Tuesday comes as higher fuel costs ripple through the airline industry.
news.why: Your travel costs are rising as airlines pass on higher fuel expenses.

news.title: All DHS workers to be paid by end of week for past 6 weeks of shutdown
news.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said DHS employees affected by the government shutdown will be paid through the recent pay periods by the end of the week.
news.why: DHS families can finally pay back rent and overdue utility bills.

news.title: Anthropic launches Project Glasswing, an effort to prevent AI cyberattacks with AI
news.description: Anthropic has announced a new initiative called Project Glasswing that aims "to secure the world’s most critical software" against AI-powered attacks.
news.why: AI-driven security is strengthening the protection of your digital data and accounts.

news.title: Toronto turning to AI to reduce traffic congestion
news.description: The City of Toronto is turning to artificial intelligence to unclog its congested streets. After a recent test, intersections in North York are being equipped with smart traffic signals.
news.why: AI-managed traffic systems could soon shorten your daily commute in major cities.

news.title: NASA releases first-ever photo of Earth from the far side of the moon
news.description: NASA unveiled the first-ever photo of Earth from the far side of the moon, dubbed "Earthset," captured by Artemis II astronauts during their lunar flyby Monday.
news.why: This tech will eventually improve GPS accuracy for your daily commute.
